content.title: Actual - Etymology, Origin & Meaning
content.text: Origin and history of actual actual(adj.)early 14c., "pertaining to acts or an action;" late 14c. in the broader sense of "real, existing" (as opposed to potential, ideal, etc.); from Old French actuel "now existing, up to date" (13c.), from Late Latin actualis "active, pertaining to action," adjectival form of Latin actus "a doing" (from PIE root *ag- "to drive, draw out or forth, move").Entries linking to actual "to make actual," 1810, first attested in Coleridge, from actual + -ize. Related: Actualized; actualizing.early 15c., "in fact, in reality" (as opposed to "in possibility"), from actual + -ly (2). The meaning "actively, vigorously" is from mid-15c.; that of "at this time, at present" is from 1660s.
